heroHeadline: Iran Counters Trump With 5-Year Enrichment Suspension Offer as US-Iran MOU Framework Nears — War Day 79; April CPI Hits 3.8% Three-Year High; Warsh-Powell Fed Showdown; Kentucky Primary Eve: Gallrein Leads Massie
heroSubtitle: Iran formally countered Trump's 20-year uranium enrichment suspension offer (announced May 15 on Air Force One) with a 5-year suspension proposal on May 18, 2026 (War Day 79) — narrowing but not closing the gap as US and Iranian officials told the Times of Israel both sides are 'closing in on a framework for a permanent deal,' with a Memorandum of Understanding being negotiated that would include an enrichment moratorium, shipment of highly-enriched uranium stockpiles out of Iran, and Washington lifting some sanctions. The naval blockade of Iranian ports continues with ~41 tankers blocked and Brent crude at ~$107/bbl. Trump gave an exclusive Fortune interview on May 18 where he said he 'should have asked for more' than a 10% Intel stake (now worth $50B+) and discussed AI policy, the Beijing summit disputes, and how the Iran war has complicated his push for Fed rate cuts. On the economy, April 2026 CPI came in at 3.8% year-over-year — a three-year high — increasing pressure on new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who faces a reported 'family fight' at the FOMC with markets giving less than 3% odds of any 2026 rate cut; former Chair Powell remains on the Board as a potential counterweight. On trade, the US-China summit dispute persisted as the White House touted soybean and rare earth deals from the Beijing summit while Chinese officials offered conflicting framing — neither Boeing nor Chinese state media confirmed the claimed 200-jet purchase. On MAGA primaries, the eve of the May 19 Kentucky Republican primary saw a final Quantus poll showing Trump-backed Ed Gallrein leading seven-term Rep. Thomas Massie 48.3% to 43.1% in the most expensive House primary in US history ($32M+ in ad spending).
